`runtime/game/smo_ui.c`:

```c
/* smo_ui.c - the game's layout textures, fonts and messages, and a small software renderer (see smo_ui.h).
 *
 * The formats, as read here (all little-endian except the Yaz0 header):
 *  Yaz0  "Yaz0", u32 big-endian decompressed size, 8 bytes; then groups of a code byte (bit set = one literal byte,
 *        clear = a back reference of 2 bytes NR RR: distance RRR + 1, length N + 2, or N = 0 and a third byte + 0x12).
 *  SARC  header of 0x14 bytes (file data offset at 0xc); SFAT: node count at +6, nodes of 16 bytes from +0xc (name hash,
 *        attributes: bit 24 = named, low 16 bits = name offset / 4 inside SFNT's names; data start, data end); SFNT:
 *        8-byte header, then the names.
 *  BNTX  "NX  " at 0x20, texture count at 0x24, offset of a table of BRTI offsets at 0x28. BRTI: tiling @0x12, mip
 *        count @0x16, format @0x1c (type << 8 | kind: 1 unorm, 2 snorm, 6 sRGB), width @0x24, height @0x28, layout
 *        word @0x34 (block height log2 in bits 0..2), channel sources @0x58 (bytes R G B A: 0 zero, 1 one, 2 R, 3 G,
 *        4 B, 5 A), name @0x60 (u16 length + characters), offset of the mip data offsets @0x70. These are the fields
 *        tests/bntx_layout_check.py compares with tex_layout for every texture of the RomFS.
 *  BFFNT version 4.1. FINF @0x14: height +9, width +10, ascent +11, line feed +12, offsets of the TGLP / CWDH / CMAP data
 *        +20 / +24 / +28 (each points 8 bytes past its section's magic). TGLP: cell width +8, cell height +9, sheet
 *        count +10, sheet size +12, baseline +16, sheet format +18 (5 LA8, 8 A8, 12 BC4), cells per row +20, rows +22,
 *        sheet width +24, height +26, data offset +28. In this game's fonts the sheet data is a BNTX of its own whose
 *        one texture is an array with a layer per sheet (otherwise: block-linear surfaces `sheet size` bytes apart),
 *        each stored with its bottom row first; glyph cells are cell size + 1 apart from the top left, in rows of
 *        `cells per row`. CWDH: first and last glyph index, next block,
 *        then (left, glyph width, advance) per glyph. CMAP: first and last code, method (0 direct, 1 table, 2 scan:
 *        u16 count, then u32 code + u16 index per 8 bytes), next block.
 *  MSBT  "MsgStdBn", section count at 0xe, sections from 0x20 (magic, size, 8 bytes, data, padded to 16): LBL1 (bucket
 *        count, buckets of count + offset, labels of u8 length + name + u32 text index), TXT2 (count, offsets, UTF-16).
 * Nothing here is game data: every byte comes from the files at run time. */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include "smo_ui.h"
#include "tex_decode.h"

const char *fs_rom_root(void);                           /* nnfs.c */

static uint16_t u16le(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint16_t)(p[0] | p[1] << 8); }
static uint32_t u32le(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24; }
static uint64_t u64le(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint64_t)u32le(p) | (uint64_t)u32le(p + 4) << 32; }

void ui_image_free(UiImage *im) { if (im) { free(im->px); memset(im, 0, sizeof *im); } }

/* ================================================================ files */
uint8_t *ui_file(const char *path, size_t *size) {
    char full[MAX_PATH];
    snprintf(full, sizeof full, "%s\\%s", fs_rom_root(), path);
    for (char *p = full; *p; p++) if (*p == '/') *p = '\\';
    FILE *f = fopen(full, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long n = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    uint8_t *b = n > 0 ? malloc((size_t)n) : NULL;
    if (b && fread(b, 1, (size_t)n, f) != (size_t)n) { free(b); b = NULL; }
    fclose(f);
    if (b && size) *size = (size_t)n;
    return b;
}

static uint8_t *yaz0(const uint8_t *s, size_t n, size_t *out) {
    if (n < 16 || memcmp(s, "Yaz0", 4)) return NULL;
    size_t size = (size_t)s[4] << 24 | (size_t)s[5] << 16 | (size_t)s[6] << 8 | s[7], si = 16, di = 0;
    uint8_t *d = malloc(size ? size : 1);
    if (!d) return NULL;
    while (di < size && si < n) {
        uint8_t code = s[si++];
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8 && di < size; bit++, code <<= 1) {
            if (code & 0x80) { if (si >= n) goto bad; d[di++] = s[si++]; continue; }
            if (si + 1 >= n) goto bad;
            size_t b1 = s[si++], b2 = s[si++], dist = ((b1 & 0xf) << 8 | b2) + 1, len = b1 >> 4;
            if (!len) { if (si >= n) goto bad; len = (size_t)s[si++] + 0x12; } else len += 2;
            if (dist > di) goto bad;
            for (; len && di < size; len--, di++) d[di] = d[di - dist];
        }
    }
    if (di != size) goto bad;
    *out = size;
    return d;
bad:
    free(d);
    return NULL;
}

uint8_t *ui_arc(const char *path, size_t *size) {
    size_t n = 0, m = 0;
    uint8_t *raw = ui_file(path, &n), *d;
    if (!raw) return NULL;
    d = yaz0(raw, n, &m);
    free(raw);
    if (d && size) *size = m;
    return d;
}

const uint8_t *ui_sarc(const uint8_t *s, size_t n, const char *name, size_t *size) {
    if (!s || n < 0x20 || memcmp(s, "SARC", 4) || u16le(s + 6) != 0xfeff) return NULL;
    size_t data = u32le(s + 0xc), sfat = u16le(s + 4);
    if (sfat + 0xc > n || memcmp(s + sfat, "SFAT", 4)) return NULL;
    int nodes = u16le(s + sfat + 6);
    size_t sfnt = sfat + 0xc + (size_t)nodes * 16;
    if (sfnt + 8 > n || memcmp(s + sfnt, "SFNT", 4)) return NULL;
    size_t names = sfnt + u16le(s + sfnt + 4);
    for (int i = 0; i < nodes; i++) {
        const uint8_t *nd = s + sfat + 0xc + (size_t)i * 16;
        uint32_t attr = u32le(nd + 4), b = u32le(nd + 8), e = u32le(nd + 12);
        if (!(attr & 0x01000000)) continue;
        size_t at = names + (size_t)(attr & 0xffff) * 4;
        if (at >= n || strncmp((const char *)s + at, name, n - at) || data + e > n || e < b) continue;
        if (size) *size = e - b;
        return s + data + b;
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* ================================================================ textures */
static int nvn_of_bntx(uint32_t fmt) {                    /* BNTX surface format -> NVN format (tex_decode.h) */
    int type = (int)(fmt >> 8), kind = (int)(fmt & 0xff), srgb = kind == 6, snorm = kind == 2;
    switch (type) {
    case 0x02: return TEX_FMT_R8;
    case 0x07: return TEX_FMT_RGB565;
    case 0x09: return TEX_FMT_RG8;
    case 0x0b: return srgb ? TEX_FMT_RGBA8_SRGB : TEX_FMT_RGBA8;
    case 0x0c: return srgb ? TEX_FMT_BGRA8_SRGB : TEX_FMT_BGRA8;
    case 0x1a: return srgb ? TEX_FMT_RGBA_DXT1_SRGB : TEX_FMT_RGBA_DXT1;
    case 0x1b: return srgb ? TEX_FMT_RGBA_DXT3_SRGB : TEX_FMT_RGBA_DXT3;
    case 0x1c: return srgb ? TEX_FMT_RGBA_DXT5_SRGB : TEX_FMT_RGBA_DXT5;
    case 0x1d: return snorm ? TEX_FMT_RGTC1_SNORM : TEX_FMT_RGTC1_UNORM;
    case 0x1e: return snorm ? TEX_FMT_RGTC2_SNORM : TEX_FMT_RGTC2_UNORM;
    case 0x20: return srgb ? TEX_FMT_BPTC_UNORM_SRGB : TEX_FMT_BPTC_UNORM;
    default:
        if (type >= 0x2d && type < 0x2d + 14) return (srgb ? TEX_FMT_ASTC_4x4_SRGB : TEX_FMT_ASTC_4x4) + (type - 0x2d);
        return -1;
    }
}

/* level 0 of a block-linear surface, decoded to RGBA8 (malloc'd); NULL if the data is short or the format unknown */
static uint8_t *decode_surface(int nvnfmt, const uint8_t *src, size_t avail, int w, int h, int mips, int bh_log2) {
    TexLayout L;
    const TexFormat *f = tex_format(nvnfmt);
    if (!f || tex_layout(&L, TEX_TARGET_2D, nvnfmt, w, h, 1, mips < 1 ? 1 : mips, 0, 0, bh_log2) < 0 || L.lvl_size[0] > avail) return NULL;
    uint8_t *lin = malloc(L.lvl_linear_size[0]), *rgba = malloc((size_t)w * h * 4);
    if (!lin || !rgba) { free(lin); free(rgba); return NULL; }
    tex_deswizzle_level(&L, 0, src, lin);
    int r = f->codec ? tex_decode_rgba8(nvnfmt, lin, w, h, rgba) : tex_convert_rgba8(nvnfmt, lin, w, h, rgba);
    free(lin);
    if (r < 0) { free(rgba); return NULL; }
    return rgba;
}

typedef struct { int fmt, w, h, mips, layers, bh; uint64_t data; uint8_t map[4]; } Brti;
/* The BRTI record named `name` (NULL: the first one) of a BNTX. 1 = found and usable. */
static int bntx_find(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, const char *name, Brti *o) {
    if (!b || n < 0x40 || memcmp(b, "BNTX", 4) || memcmp(b + 0x20, "NX  ", 4)) return 0;
    uint32_t count = u32le(b + 0x24);
    uint64_t table = u64le(b + 0x28);
    if (table + (uint64_t)count * 8 > n) return 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        uint64_t t = u64le(b + table + (uint64_t)i * 8);
        if (t + 0x78 > n || memcmp(b + t, "BRTI", 4)) continue;
        if (name) {
            uint64_t name_at = u64le(b + t + 0x60);
            if (name_at + 2 > n) continue;
            size_t len = u16le(b + name_at);
            if (name_at + 2 + len > n || len != strlen(name) || memcmp(b + name_at + 2, name, len)) continue;
        }
        uint64_t ptrs = u64le(b + t + 0x70);
        o->fmt = nvn_of_bntx(u32le(b + t + 0x1c));
        o->mips = u16le(b + t + 0x16); o->w = (int)u32le(b + t + 0x24); o->h = (int)u32le(b + t + 0x28);
        o->layers = (int)u32le(b + t + 0x30); o->bh = (int)(u32le(b + t + 0x34) & 7);
        memcpy(o->map, b + t + 0x58, 4);
        if (o->layers < 1) o->layers = 1;
        if (u16le(b + t + 0x12) != 0 || o->fmt < 0 || o->w <= 0 || o->h <= 0 || o->w > 8192 || o->h > 8192 || ptrs + 8 > n) return 0;
        o->data = u64le(b + ptrs);
        return o->data < n;
    }
    return 0;
}
/* one layer of a BRTI, level 0, decoded to RGBA8 (before the channel mapping) */
static uint8_t *bntx_layer(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, const Brti *t, int layer) {
    TexLayout L;
    if (tex_layout(&L, t->layers > 1 ? TEX_TARGET_2D_ARRAY : TEX_TARGET_2D, t->fmt, t->w, t->h, t->layers, t->mips < 1 ? 1 : t->mips, 0, 0, t->bh) < 0) return NULL;
    uint64_t at = t->data + (uint64_t)layer * L.layer_stride;
    if (layer >= t->layers || at >= n) return NULL;
    return decode_surface(t->fmt, b + at, n - at, t->w, t->h, t->mips, t->bh);
}

int ui_bntx(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, const char *name, UiImage *out) {
    Brti t;
    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
    if (!bntx_find(b, n, name, &t)) return 0;
    uint8_t *rgba = bntx_layer(b, n, &t, 0);
    if (!rgba) return 0;
    for (size_t p = 0; p < (size_t)t.w * t.h; p++) {        /* the texture's channel sources, then alpha premultiplied */
        uint8_t *q = rgba + p * 4, v[4];
        for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) v[k] = t.map[k] == 0 ? 0 : t.map[k] == 1 ? 255 : t.map[k] <= 5 ? q[t.map[k] - 2] : q[k];
        for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) q[k] = (uint8_t)((v[k] * v[3] + 127) / 255);
        q[3] = v[3];
    }
    out->w = t.w; out->h = t.h; out->ch = 4; out->px = rgba;
    return 1;
}

/* ================================================================ fonts */
typedef struct { uint32_t code; uint16_t index; } CodeMap;
typedef struct { uint16_t first, last; const int8_t *w; } WidthBlock;   /* w: 3 bytes per glyph, into the copy */
struct UiFont {
    uint8_t *file;                                         /* a copy of the BFFNT (CWDH data points into it) */
    UiImage *sheets;
    int nsheets, cell_w, cell_h, baseline, cols, rows, height, ascent, linefeed;
    int8_t def_w[3];
    CodeMap *map; int nmap;
    WidthBlock *wb; int nwb;
};
static int map_cmp(const void *a, const void *b) { uint32_t x = ((const CodeMap *)a)->code, y = ((const CodeMap *)b)->code; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }

UiFont *ui_font(const uint8_t *src, size_t n) {
    if (!src || n < 0x60 || memcmp(src, "FFNT", 4) || u16le(src + 4) != 0xfeff) return NULL;
    UiFont *f = calloc(1, sizeof *f);
    uint8_t *b = f ? malloc(n) : NULL;
    if (!b) { free(f); return NULL; }
    memcpy(b, src, n);
    f->file = b;
    const uint8_t *finf = b + u16le(b + 6);
    if (finf + 0x20 > b + n || memcmp(finf, "FINF", 4)) goto bad;
    f->height = finf[9]; f->ascent = finf[11]; f->linefeed = u16le(finf + 12);
    memcpy(f->def_w, finf + 16, 3);
    size_t tg = u32le(finf + 20) - 8, cw = u32le(finf + 24) - 8, cm = u32le(finf + 28) - 8;
    if (tg + 0x20 > n || memcmp(b + tg, "TGLP", 4)) goto bad;
    const uint8_t *t = b + tg;
    f->cell_w = t[8]; f->cell_h = t[9]; f->nsheets = t[10];
    size_t sheet_size = u32le(t + 12), data = u32le(t + 28);
    int fmt = u16le(t + 18) & 0x3fff, sw = u16le(t + 24), sh = u16le(t + 26);
    f->baseline = u16le(t + 16); f->cols = u16le(t + 20); f->rows = u16le(t + 22);
    if (f->nsheets <= 0 || f->cols <= 0 || f->rows <= 0 || data + sheet_size * (size_t)f->nsheets > n) goto bad;
    f->sheets = calloc((size_t)f->nsheets, sizeof *f->sheets);
    if (!f->sheets) goto bad;
    Brti arr;                                              /* the sheets: one texture array in a BNTX of their own */
    int in_bntx = bntx_find(b + data, n - data, NULL, &arr) && arr.w == sw && arr.h == sh && arr.layers >= f->nsheets;
    for (int s = 0; s < f->nsheets; s++) {
        int nvnfmt = fmt == 12 ? TEX_FMT_RGTC1_UNORM : fmt == 8 ? TEX_FMT_R8 : fmt == 5 ? TEX_FMT_RG8 : -1;
        uint8_t *rgba = in_bntx ? bntx_layer(b + data, n - data, &arr, s)
                      : nvnfmt < 0 ? NULL : decode_surface(nvnfmt, b + data + sheet_size * (size_t)s, sheet_size, sw, sh, 1, -1);
        if (!rgba) { printf("ui: font sheet format %d not supported or short\n", fmt); goto bad; }
        UiImage *im = &f->sheets[s];
        im->w = sw; im->h = sh; im->ch = 1; im->px = malloc((size_t)sw * sh);
        if (!im->px) { free(rgba); goto bad; }
        for (int y = 0; y < sh; y++)                       /* the sheets are stored bottom row first: turned upright here */
            for (int x = 0; x < sw; x++) im->px[(size_t)y * sw + x] = rgba[((size_t)(sh - 1 - y) * sw + x) * 4 + (fmt == 5 ? 1 : 0)];   /* BC4 / A8: R; LA8: the second byte */
        free(rgba);
    }
    for (size_t p = cw; p && p + 8 <= n && f->nwb < 64; ) {   /* CWDH blocks */
        if (memcmp(b + p, "CWDH", 4)) break;
        WidthBlock *nw = realloc(f->wb, sizeof *f->wb * (size_t)(f->nwb + 1));
        if (!nw) break;
        f->wb = nw;
        f->wb[f->nwb].first = u16le(b + p + 8); f->wb[f->nwb].last = u16le(b + p + 10); f->wb[f->nwb].w = (const int8_t *)(b + p + 16);
        if (p + 16 + 3u * (size_t)(f->wb[f->nwb].last - f->wb[f->nwb].first + 1) > n) break;
        f->nwb++;
        size_t next = u32le(b + p + 12);
        p = next ? next - 8 : 0;
    }
    for (size_t p = cm; p && p + 24 <= n; ) {               /* CMAP blocks */
        if (memcmp(b + p, "CMAP", 4)) break;
        uint32_t first = u32le(b + p + 8), last = u32le(b + p + 12);
        int method = u16le(b + p + 16);
        const uint8_t *d = b + p + 24;
        size_t add = method == 2 ? u16le(d) : last >= first ? (size_t)(last - first + 1) : 0, k = (size_t)f->nmap;
        CodeMap *nm = realloc(f->map, sizeof *f->map * (k + add + 1));
        if (!nm) break;
        f->map = nm;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < add; i++) {
            uint32_t code; uint16_t idx;
            if (method == 0) { code = first + (uint32_t)i; idx = (uint16_t)(u16le(d) + i); }
            else if (method == 1) { code = first + (uint32_t)i; idx = u16le(d + 2 * i); }
            else { code = u32le(d + 4 + 8 * i); idx = u16le(d + 8 + 8 * i); }
            if (idx != 0xffff) { f->map[k].code = code; f->map[k].index = idx; k++; }
        }
        f->nmap = (int)k;
        size_t next = u32le(b + p + 20);
        p = next ? next - 8 : 0;
    }
    qsort(f->map, (size_t)f->nmap, sizeof *f->map, map_cmp);
    return f;
bad:
    ui_font_free(f);
    return NULL;
}
void ui_font_free(UiFont *f) {
    if (!f) return;
    for (int s = 0; f->sheets && s < f->nsheets; s++) ui_image_free(&f->sheets[s]);
    free(f->sheets); free(f->map); free(f->wb); free(f->file); free(f);
}
void ui_font_info(const UiFont *f, UiFontInfo *o) {
    o->height = f->height; o->ascent = f->ascent; o->linefeed = f->linefeed;
    o->cell_w = f->cell_w; o->cell_h = f->cell_h; o->baseline = f->baseline;
}
static int glyph_of(const UiFont *f, uint32_t code) {
    int lo = 0, hi = f->nmap - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
        if (f->map[mid].code == code) return f->map[mid].index;
        if (f->map[mid].code < code) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;
    }
    return -1;
}
static void widths_of(const UiFont *f, int g, int8_t out[3]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < f->nwb; i++)
        if (g >= f->wb[i].first && g <= f->wb[i].last) { memcpy(out, f->wb[i].w + 3 * (g - f->wb[i].first), 3); return; }
    memcpy(out, f->def_w, 3);
}

/* ================================================================ messages */
struct UiMsbt { int n; char **labels; uint16_t **texts; int *index; int ntexts; };
UiMsbt *ui_msbt(const uint8_t *b, size_t n) {
    if (!b || n < 0x20 || memcmp(b, "MsgStdBn", 8) || b[8] != 0xff || b[9] != 0xfe) return NULL;   /* little-endian only */
    UiMsbt *m = calloc(1, sizeof *m);
    if (!m) return NULL;
    int sections = u16le(b + 0xe);
    size_t p = 0x20;
    for (int s = 0; s < sections && p + 16 <= n; s++) {
        size_t size = u32le(b + p + 4);
        const uint8_t *d = b + p + 16;
        if (p + 16 + size > n) break;
        if (!memcmp(b + p, "LBL1", 4) && size >= 4) {
            uint32_t buckets = u32le(d);
            for (uint32_t k = 0; k < buckets && 4 + 8 * (size_t)k + 8 <= size; k++) {
                uint32_t cnt = u32le(d + 4 + 8 * k), at = u32le(d + 8 + 8 * k);
                for (uint32_t j = 0; j < cnt && at < size; j++) {
                    size_t len = d[at];
                    if (at + 1 + len + 4 > size) break;
                    char **nl = realloc(m->labels, sizeof *m->labels * (size_t)(m->n + 1));
                    int *ni = realloc(m->index, sizeof *m->index * (size_t)(m->n + 1));
                    if (nl) m->labels = nl;
                    if (ni) m->index = ni;
                    if (!nl || !ni) break;
                    m->labels[m->n] = malloc(len + 1);
                    if (!m->labels[m->n]) break;
                    memcpy(m->labels[m->n], d + at + 1, len); m->labels[m->n][len] = 0;
                    m->index[m->n] = (int)u32le(d + at + 1 + len);
                    m->n++;
                    at += (uint32_t)(1 + len + 4);
                }
            }
        } else if (!memcmp(b + p, "TXT2", 4) && size >= 4) {
            uint32_t cnt = u32le(d);
            if (4 + 4 * (size_t)cnt > size) break;
            m->texts = calloc(cnt ? cnt : 1, sizeof *m->texts);
            if (!m->texts) break;
            m->ntexts = (int)cnt;
            for (uint32_t k = 0; k < cnt; k++) {
                size_t a = u32le(d + 4 + 4 * k), e = k + 1 < cnt ? u32le(d + 8 + 4 * k) : size;
                if (a > size || e > size || e < a) e = a;
                size_t chars = (e - a) / 2;
                m->texts[k] = calloc(chars + 1, 2);
                if (!m->texts[k]) continue;
                for (size_t i = 0; i < chars; i++) m->texts[k][i] = u16le(d + a + 2 * i);
            }
        }
        p += 16 + ((size + 15) & ~(size_t)15);
    }
    for (int i = 1; i < m->n; i++)                         /* the labels in the order of their texts (LBL1 keeps them by hash) */
        for (int k = i; k > 0 && m->index[k - 1] > m->index[k]; k--) {
            char *l = m->labels[k]; m->labels[k] = m->labels[k - 1]; m->labels[k - 1] = l;
            int x = m->index[k]; m->index[k] = m->index[k - 1]; m->index[k - 1] = x;
        }
    return m;
}
void ui_msbt_free(UiMsbt *m) {
    if (!m) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < m->n; i++) free(m->labels[i]);
    for (int i = 0; i < m->ntexts; i++) free(m->texts[i]);
    free(m->labels); free(m->index); free(m->texts); free(m);
}
int ui_msbt_count(const UiMsbt *m) { return m ? m->n : 0; }
const char *ui_msbt_label(const UiMsbt *m, int i) { return m && i >= 0 && i < m->n ? m->labels[i] : NULL; }
const uint16_t *ui_msbt_text_at(const UiMsbt *m, int i) {
    if (!m || i < 0 || i >= m->n || m->index[i] < 0 || m->index[i] >= m->ntexts) return NULL;
    return m->texts[m->index[i]];
}
const uint16_t *ui_msbt_text(const UiMsbt *m, const char *label) {
    for (int i = 0; m && i < m->n; i++) if (!strcmp(m->labels[i], label)) return ui_msbt_text_at(m, i);
    return NULL;
}

/* ================================================================ drawing */
UiXf ui_xf_screen(int w, int h) { UiXf x = {(float)w / 1280.0f, 0, (float)w * 0.5f, 0, -(float)h / 720.0f, (float)h * 0.5f}; return x; }
UiXf ui_xf_mul(UiXf o, UiXf i) {
    UiXf r = {o.a * i.a + o.b * i.d, o.a * i.b + o.b * i.e, o.a * i.c + o.b * i.f + o.c,
              o.d * i.a + o.e * i.d, o.d * i.b + o.e * i.e, o.d * i.c + o.e * i.f + o.f};
    return r;
}
UiXf ui_xf_move(float x, float y) { UiXf r = {1, 0, x, 0, 1, y}; return r; }
UiXf ui_xf_rotate(float deg) { float s = sinf(deg * 3.14159265f / 180.0f), c = cosf(deg * 3.14159265f / 180.0f); UiXf r = {c, -s, 0, s, c, 0}; return r; }
UiXf ui_xf_scale(float sx, float sy) { UiXf r = {sx, 0, 0, 0, sy, 0}; return r; }

static inline float clamp01(float v) { return v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v; }

void ui_draw(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, const UiImage *src, float u0, float v0, float u1, float v1, uint32_t rgba) {
    ui_draw_edges(dst, xf, x0, y0, x1, y1, src, u0, v0, u1, v1, rgba, UI_EDGE_ALL);
}
void ui_draw_edges(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, const UiImage *src, float u0, float v0, float u1, float v1, uint32_t rgba, int edges) {
    if (!dst || !dst->px || x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0) return;
    float det = xf.a * xf.e - xf.b * xf.d;
    if (fabsf(det) < 1e-12f) return;
    float ia = xf.e / det, ib = -xf.b / det, id = -xf.d / det, ie = xf.a / det;
    float kx = sqrtf(xf.a * xf.a + xf.d * xf.d), ky = sqrtf(xf.b * xf.b + xf.e * xf.e);     /* pixels per unit along the rectangle's axes */
    float cx[4] = {x0, x1, x1, x0}, cy[4] = {y0, y0, y1, y1}, minx = 1e30f, maxx = -1e30f, miny = 1e30f, maxy = -1e30f;
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
        float X = xf.a * cx[k] + xf.b * cy[k] + xf.c, Y = xf.d * cx[k] + xf.e * cy[k] + xf.f;
        if (X < minx) minx = X; if (X > maxx) maxx = X; if (Y < miny) miny = Y; if (Y > maxy) maxy = Y;
    }
    int bx0 = (int)floorf(minx) - 1, bx1 = (int)ceilf(maxx) + 1, by0 = (int)floorf(miny) - 1, by1 = (int)ceilf(maxy) + 1;
    if (bx0 < 0) bx0 = 0; if (by0 < 0) by0 = 0; if (bx1 > dst->w) bx1 = dst->w; if (by1 > dst->h) by1 = dst->h;
    float cr = (float)(rgba >> 24) / 255.0f, cg = (float)((rgba >> 16) & 255) / 255.0f, cb = (float)((rgba >> 8) & 255) / 255.0f, ca = (float)(rgba & 255) / 255.0f;
    float du = (u1 - u0) / (x1 - x0), dv = (v1 - v0) / (y1 - y0);
    for (int Y = by0; Y < by1; Y++) {
        uint8_t *row = dst->px + (size_t)Y * dst->w * 4;
        for (int X = bx0; X < bx1; X++) {
            float px = (float)X + 0.5f - xf.c, py = (float)Y + 0.5f - xf.f;
            float lx = ia * px + ib * py, ly = id * px + ie * py;
            /* coverage: smooth over a pixel at the edges in `edges`, a hard half-open step at the others (pieces of one shape
             * that share an edge then cover each pixel once, without a seam) */
            float el = edges & UI_EDGE_LEFT ? clamp01((lx - x0) * kx + 0.5f) : (float)(lx >= x0), er = edges & UI_EDGE_RIGHT ? clamp01((x1 - lx) * kx + 0.5f) : (float)(lx < x1);
            float eb = edges & UI_EDGE_BOTTOM ? clamp01((ly - y0) * ky + 0.5f) : (float)(ly >= y0), et = edges & UI_EDGE_TOP ? clamp01((y1 - ly) * ky + 0.5f) : (float)(ly < y1);
            float cov = (el < er ? el : er) * (eb < et ? eb : et);
            if (cov <= 0.0f) continue;
            float sr = 1, sg = 1, sb = 1, sa = 1;
            if (src) {
                float tu = u0 + (lx - x0) * du - 0.5f, tv = v0 + (y1 - ly) * dv - 0.5f;
                int ix = (int)floorf(tu), iy = (int)floorf(tv);
                float fx = tu - (float)ix, fy = tv - (float)iy, acc[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
                for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
                    int sx = ix + (k & 1), sy = iy + (k >> 1);
                    float wgt = ((k & 1) ? fx : 1 - fx) * ((k >> 1) ? fy : 1 - fy);
                    if (sx < 0) sx = 0; if (sy < 0) sy = 0; if (sx >= src->w) sx = src->w - 1; if (sy >= src->h) sy = src->h - 1;
                    if (src->ch == 1) acc[3] += wgt * src->px[(size_t)sy * src->w + sx];
                    else { const uint8_t *q = src->px + ((size_t)sy * src->w + sx) * 4; for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) acc[c] += wgt * q[c]; }
                }
                if (src->ch == 1) { sa = acc[3] / 255.0f; sr = sg = sb = sa; }
                else { sr = acc[0] / 255.0f; sg = acc[1] / 255.0f; sb = acc[2] / 255.0f; sa = acc[3] / 255.0f; }
            }
            float a = sa * ca * cov;                          /* premultiplied source times the colour */
            if (a <= 0.0f) continue;
            float r = sr * cr * ca * cov, g = sg * cg * ca * cov, bl = sb * cb * ca * cov, keep = 1.0f - a;
            uint8_t *q = row + (size_t)X * 4;
            q[0] = (uint8_t)(clamp01(r + (float)q[0] / 255.0f * keep) * 255.0f + 0.5f);
            q[1] = (uint8_t)(clamp01(g + (float)q[1] / 255.0f * keep) * 255.0f + 0.5f);
            q[2] = (uint8_t)(clamp01(bl + (float)q[2] / 255.0f * keep) * 255.0f + 0.5f);
            q[3] = (uint8_t)(clamp01(a + (float)q[3] / 255.0f * keep) * 255.0f + 0.5f);
        }
    }
}

/* The picture of a device icon tag (group 6) in the console's private-use font area: the type numbers are the ones the
 * game's footers use (Footer.msbt: 2 with A, 3 with B, 5 with Y, 16 with the left stick, 17 with the right stick). */
static uint32_t icon_code(int group, int type) {
    if (group != 6) return 0;
    switch (type) {
    case 2: return 0xe0e0;   /* A */
    case 3: return 0xe0e1;   /* B */
    case 4: return 0xe0e2;   /* X */
    case 5: return 0xe0e3;   /* Y */
    case 16: return 0xe101;  /* left stick */
    case 17: return 0xe102;  /* right stick */
    default: return 0;
    }
}

static float glyph(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, const UiFont *f, int g, float x, float y, float scale, uint32_t rgba) {
    int8_t w[3];
    widths_of(f, g, w);
    int per = f->cols * f->rows, sheet = g / per, cell = g % per, col = cell % f->cols, row = cell / f->cols;
    if (dst && sheet < f->nsheets && (uint8_t)w[1]) {
        float u = (float)(col * (f->cell_w + 1)), v = (float)(row * (f->cell_h + 1));
        float gx = x + (float)w[0] * scale, top = y + (float)f->baseline * scale;
        ui_draw(dst, xf, gx, top - (float)f->cell_h * scale, gx + (float)(uint8_t)w[1] * scale, top, &f->sheets[sheet], u, v, u + (float)(uint8_t)w[1], v + (float)f->cell_h, rgba);
    }
    return (float)(uint8_t)w[2] * scale;
}

float ui_text(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, const UiFont *f, const UiFont *icons, const uint16_t *s, int len, float x, float y, float scale, uint32_t rgba) {
    float pen = x;
    if (!f || !s) return 0;
    for (int i = 0; len < 0 ? s[i] != 0 : i < len; i++) {
        uint16_t ch = s[i];
        if (ch == 0x0e) {                                  /* tag: group, type, payload size in bytes, payload */
            int group = s[i + 1], type = s[i + 2], size = s[i + 3];
            uint32_t code = icon_code(group, type);
            i += 3 + size / 2;
            int gi = icons && code ? glyph_of(icons, code) : -1;
            if (gi >= 0) {                                 /* the icon's cell as high as the text's line, centred on its capitals */
                float k = scale * (float)f->height / (float)icons->cell_h;
                float base = y + 0.33f * ((float)f->ascent * scale - (float)icons->ascent * k);
                pen += glyph(dst, xf, icons, gi, pen, base, k, rgba);
            }
            continue;
        }
        if (ch == 0x0f) { i += 2; continue; }             /* end of a tag: group, type */
        if (ch == '\n' || ch == '\r') break;
        int gi = glyph_of(f, ch);
        if (gi < 0) gi = glyph_of(f, '?');
        if (gi >= 0) pen += glyph(dst, xf, f, gi, pen, y, scale, rgba);
    }
    return pen - x;
}

```

`runtime/game/smo_ui.h`:

```h
/* smo_ui.h - menus the runtime draws itself, in the look of the game's own menus.
 *
 * Everything shown is the game's: its layout textures (BNTX in the layout archives), its fonts (BFFNT), its message
 * files (MSBT), read at run time from the RomFS the runtime mounts (nnfs.c; extracted from the user's own dump, never
 * stored by this project). The drawing is done in host memory: affine textured rectangles with bilinear sampling and
 * anti-aliased edges, blended over a frame; smo_amiibo.c composes its menu with it and nvn_vk_draw.c shows the frame.
 *
 * Coordinates: the game's layouts place their panes in a 1280 x 720 space with the origin at the centre and y up;
 * ui_xf_screen maps that space onto a frame of any size. */
#ifndef SMO_UI_H
#define SMO_UI_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* An image in host memory, rows from the top. ch = 4: RGBA8, alpha premultiplied; ch = 1: coverage (font sheets). */
typedef struct { int w, h, ch; uint8_t *px; } UiImage;
void ui_image_free(UiImage *im);

/* ---- the game's files (NULL when missing; the results are malloc'd unless said otherwise) */
uint8_t *ui_file(const char *path, size_t *size);                                    /* a file of the RomFS, '/' separated */
uint8_t *ui_arc(const char *path, size_t *size);                                     /* a Yaz0-compressed archive of the RomFS, decompressed */
const uint8_t *ui_sarc(const uint8_t *sarc, size_t n, const char *name, size_t *size);   /* a file inside a SARC: points into it */

/* ---- textures: level 0 of the BNTX texture `name`, decoded, with the texture's channel mapping. 1 = done */
int ui_bntx(const uint8_t *bntx, size_t n, const char *name, UiImage *out);

/* ---- fonts (BFFNT, glyph sheets in BC4 / A8 / LA8) */
typedef struct UiFont UiFont;
UiFont *ui_font(const uint8_t *bffnt, size_t n);
void ui_font_free(UiFont *f);
typedef struct { int height, ascent, linefeed, cell_w, cell_h, baseline; } UiFontInfo;   /* FINF and TGLP, in font pixels */
void ui_font_info(const UiFont *f, UiFontInfo *out);

/* ---- messages (MSBT): labels in the order of their texts; texts keep their tags (0x0E group type size payload, 0x0F group type) */
typedef struct UiMsbt UiMsbt;
UiMsbt *ui_msbt(const uint8_t *msbt, size_t n);
void ui_msbt_free(UiMsbt *m);
int ui_msbt_count(const UiMsbt *m);
const char *ui_msbt_label(const UiMsbt *m, int i);
const uint16_t *ui_msbt_text_at(const UiMsbt *m, int i);
const uint16_t *ui_msbt_text(const UiMsbt *m, const char *label);                    /* NULL = no such label */

/* ---- drawing */
typedef struct { float a, b, c, d, e, f; } UiXf;           /* x' = a x + b y + c, y' = d x + e y + f */
UiXf ui_xf_screen(int w, int h);                           /* layout space -> pixels of a w x h frame */

UiXf ui_xf_move(float x, float y);
UiXf ui_xf_rotate(float degrees);                          /* counter-clockwise with y up, as a pane's z rotation */
UiXf ui_xf_scale(float sx, float sy);
/* The rectangle [x0,x1] x [y0,y1] (through xf) filled with the texels [u0,u1] x [v0,v1] of src (v down; u0 > u1 mirrors;
 * src NULL = plain), times rgba (0xRRGGBBAA, not premultiplied), blended over dst. */
void ui_draw(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, const UiImage *src, float u0, float v0, float u1, float v1, uint32_t rgba);
/* the same with anti-aliasing only on the edges named (UI_EDGE_*): the inner edges of pieces of one shape */
enum { UI_EDGE_LEFT = 1, UI_EDGE_RIGHT = 2, UI_EDGE_BOTTOM = 4, UI_EDGE_TOP = 8, UI_EDGE_ALL = 15 };
void ui_draw_edges(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, const UiImage *src, float u0, float v0, float u1, float v1, uint32_t rgba, int edges);
/* One line of text, pen at (x, y) on the baseline, `scale` layout units per font pixel; len < 0 = up to the 0. Device icon
 * tags (group 6: the button and stick pictures of the footers) are drawn from `icons`, their cells as high as the text's
 * line; other tags are skipped. Returns the advance. dst NULL = measure only. */
float ui_text(UiImage *dst, UiXf xf, const UiFont *f, const UiFont *icons, const uint16_t *s, int len, float x, float y, float scale, uint32_t rgba);

/* ---- showing a menu: what smo_amiibo.c asks the render back end (RBackend.menu, nvn_vk_draw.c) on the render thread */
enum { UI_MENU_READ, UI_MENU_SHOW, UI_MENU_END };
typedef struct {
    int op;                     /* READ: the frame just presented, read back; SHOW: rgba over the whole window; END: free what SHOW made */
    void *present;              /* the PresentJob of that frame (nvn_front.h) */
    const uint8_t *rgba;        /* SHOW: w x h RGBA8, in the colour encoding of the frame READ gave */
    int w, h, changed;          /* SHOW: changed = 0: the picture of the previous SHOW again */
    uint8_t *out;               /* READ: malloc'd w x h RGBA8 (alpha 255), freed by the caller */
    int out_w, out_h, ok;
} UiMenuJob;
#endif
```

`runtime/gfx/display.c`:

```c
/* Host display: a real window, 60 Hz pacing and the guest's vsync event.
 * The window's contents are drawn by the graphics layer's render thread (nvn_gl.c's front end; Vulkan by default). */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include "runtime.h"
#include "hostrt.h"
#include "gfx_options.h"

#define A0 (c->x[0])
#define A1 (c->x[1])
#define RET(v) (c->x[0] = (uint64_t)(v))
#define WIDTH 1280
#define HEIGHT 720
#define FRAME_NS 16666667LL

void os_init_event(uint64_t key, int autoclear);      /* os_threads.c */
void os_signal_event(uint64_t key);

static HWND g_hwnd;
static volatile LONG g_ready;
static volatile LONG64 g_frames;
void nvn_gl_start(void *hwnd);                        /* nvn_gl.c */
void nvn_gl_report(FILE *out);
void nvn_tl(int ev, int arg);                          /* nvn_gl.c: SMO_FRAMETL timeline */
static uint64_t g_vsync_event;
static LARGE_INTEGER g_freq;

/* ONE refresh clock. The game counts the signals of the vsync event on a thread of its own ("VSync Count
 * Thread", 0x7103810a40: window object + 0x138) and, at every present (0x710386fc30), advances its frame counter
 * (0x710593a440) by the number of refreshes counted since the previous present. So the refresh count IS the game's
 * time. Before this, the event came from a Sleep() loop and presentation was held by a second, independent 60 Hz
 * clock that restarted its phase after every late frame: between two presents the game counted 0, 1 or 2 refreshes,
 * and "0" counts as one step while "2" counts as two, so the game's clock gained (10.77 s per 600 frames; measured by
 * ssbu-recomp in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, whose main the addresses above are in).
 * Now: refresh n happens at t0 + n/60 s; at each one the vsync event is signalled and then the frames waiting to be
 * shown are released. A frame queued between refresh n and n+1 is shown at n+1, and no sooner than `interval`
 * refreshes after the frame before it (nvnWindowSetPresentInterval); the game is held in its wait for the window
 * texture (nvnSyncWait on the sync of nvnWindowAcquireTexture), which is AFTER it has read the refresh count, as on
 * the console. SMO_OLD_PACING=1: the two clocks as before. SMO_CLOCKSTAT=1: one line every 600 presented frames. */
static int g_old_pacing = -1, g_clockstat;
static volatile LONG64 g_vsync_n;            /* refreshes passed (published after the event was signalled) */
static volatile LONG64 g_vsync_signals, g_vsync_late;
static SRWLOCK g_vsync_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
static CONDITION_VARIABLE g_vsync_cv = CONDITION_VARIABLE_INIT;
static LONG64 g_latch;                       /* refresh at which the last queued frame is shown */
static volatile LONG g_latch_pending;        /* a frame was queued and nobody has waited for its refresh yet */
static int old_pacing(void) {
    if (g_old_pacing < 0) { const char *e = getenv("SMO_OLD_PACING"); g_old_pacing = e && atoi(e) != 0; g_clockstat = getenv("SMO_CLOCKSTAT") && atoi(getenv("SMO_CLOCKSTAT")) != 0; }
    return g_old_pacing;
}
static void vsync_test_key(void);

/* while the amiibo menu (smo_amiibo.c) holds the game, the game's vsync event is not signalled: its VSync Count
 * Thread would count every refresh of the wait and the game would step that many frames at once when it goes on. The menu
 * paces itself on the same refresh clock (display_menu_wait). */
static volatile LONG g_menu_hold;
void display_menu_hold(int on) { InterlockedExchange(&g_menu_hold, on); }
int display_menu_held(void) { return g_menu_hold != 0; }     /* nvn_vk_watchdog.c: a game held on purpose (menu, guide) is not frozen */
static int vsync_signal_ok(void) { return !g_menu_hold; }

/* TEST ONLY, SMO_SPEED=<n>: the refresh clock (vsync_thread) runs n times faster, 60 x n refreshes a second (any number
 * > 0; 0 = 960 a second, as fast as the PC can run the game). The game waits for a refresh before each frame and steps
 * once per frame, so it runs up to n times faster where the PC keeps up; input sequences count frames, so they play the
 * same. Not set or 1 = nothing changes. (A lockstep clock, a refresh only once the game has queued a frame, never starts
 * this game: it waits for a refresh before its first frame.) */
static double g_rate = 60.0;                          /* refreshes a second */
static void speed_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("SMO_SPEED");
    if (!e || !e[0]) return;
    double speed = atof(e);
    g_rate = speed > 0 ? 60.0 * speed : 960.0;
    if (g_rate != 60.0) printf("display: SMO_SPEED=%s (TEST ONLY): the refresh clock runs at %.0f Hz\n", e, g_rate);
}

int oe_exit_request(void);                            /* nnmisc.c */
static volatile LONG g_closing;
int display_closing(void) { return g_closing != 0; }  /* smo_amiibo.c: the menu gives way to the game when the window is being closed */

/* The window's mode (config\graphics.ini, gfx_options.c): windowed, borderless fullscreen, fullscreen (topmost), or the
 * default, a borderless window of the configured size (dragged anywhere to move it). F11, or a double-click in a borderless
 * window, switches between covering the monitor and the window; a window left by a mode that started covering the monitor
 * is the borderless window of the configured size, centred. Called on the window thread. */
static int g_win_full;                                /* the window covers its monitor now */
static int g_win_drag;                                /* the window is a borderless window now: its whole area moves it */
static int g_win_topmost;                             /* graphics.ini fullscreen: covering the monitor means on top */
static RECT g_win_rect;                               /* the window's rectangle (and style) before it covered the monitor */
static DWORD g_win_style;
static void window_fullscreen(HWND h, int on) {
    MONITORINFO mi;
    memset(&mi, 0, sizeof mi); mi.cbSize = sizeof mi;
    if (on == g_win_full || !GetMonitorInfoA(MonitorFromWindow(h, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST), &mi)) return;
    if (on) {
        GetWindowRect(h, &g_win_rect);
        g_win_style = (DWORD)GetWindowLongA(h, GWL_STYLE);
        SetWindowLongA(h, GWL_STYLE, (LONG)((g_win_style & ~(DWORD)WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW) | WS_POPUP | WS_VISIBLE));
        SetWindowPos(h, g_win_topmost ? HWND_TOPMOST : HWND_TOP, mi.rcMonitor.left, mi.rcMonitor.top, mi.rcMonitor.right - mi.rcMonitor.left,
                     mi.rcMonitor.bottom - mi.rcMonitor.top, SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOOWNERZORDER | SWP_SHOWWINDOW);
        g_win_drag = 0;
    } else {
        if (IsRectEmpty(&g_win_rect)) {
            const GfxOptions *go = gfx_options();
            int ww = mi.rcWork.right - mi.rcWork.left, wh = mi.rcWork.bottom - mi.rcWork.top;
            int cw = go->width < ww ? go->width : ww, ch = go->height < wh ? go->height : wh;
            SetRect(&g_win_rect, mi.rcWork.left + (ww - cw) / 2, mi.rcWork.top + (wh - ch) / 2, mi.rcWork.left + (ww - cw) / 2 + cw, mi.rcWork.top + (wh - ch) / 2 + ch);
            g_win_style = WS_POPUP | WS_CLIPCHILDREN;
        }
        SetWindowLongA(h, GWL_STYLE, (LONG)(g_win_style | WS_VISIBLE));
        SetWindowPos(h, HWND_NOTOPMOST, g_win_rect.left, g_win_rect.top, g_win_rect.right - g_win_rect.left, g_win_rect.bottom - g_win_rect.top,
                     SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOOWNERZORDER | SWP_SHOWWINDOW);
        g_win_drag = !(g_win_style & WS_CAPTION);
    }
    g_win_full = on;
    printf("display: the window %s (F11)\n", on ? "covers its monitor" : g_win_drag ? "is a borderless window" : "has its frame again");
    fflush(stdout);
}

void *display_hwnd(void) { return g_hwnd; }
void display_toggle_fullscreen(void) { if (g_hwnd) window_fullscreen(g_hwnd, !g_win_full); }    /* on the window thread (smo_guide.c) */
#define WM_SMO_GUIDE (WM_APP + 0x47)                /* smo_guide.c: the Help page in the game window */
void guide_on_message(HWND hwnd, WPARAM what, LPARAM arg);
void guide_on_size(void);

static LRESULT CALLBACK wndproc(HWND h, UINT m, WPARAM w, LPARAM l) {
    if (m == WM_SMO_GUIDE) { guide_on_message(h, w, l); return 0; }
    if (m == WM_SIZE) guide_on_size();
    if (m == WM_NCHITTEST && g_win_drag) {           /* a borderless window: dragging anywhere moves it */
        LRESULT r = DefWindowProcA(h, m, w, l);
        return r == HTCLIENT ? HTCAPTION : r;
    }
    if ((m == WM_NCLBUTTONDBLCLK && w == HTCAPTION && g_win_drag) || (m == WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK && g_win_full)) { window_fullscreen(h, !g_win_full); return 0; }
    if (m == WM_KEYDOWN && w == VK_F11 && !(l & (1 << 30))) { window_fullscreen(h, !g_win_full); return 0; }
    if (m == WM_CLOSE) {                             /* the exit request: nn::oe decides (nnmisc.c oe_exit_request) whether the game ends now or after its exit-request handling section */
        InterlockedExchange(&g_closing, 1);
        printf("\nwindow closed by the user after %lld frames\n", (long long)g_frames);
        if (!oe_exit_request()) report_and_exit(0);
        return 0;
    }
    if (m == WM_ERASEBKGND) return 1;
    if (m == WM_KEYDOWN && w == VK_F12 && !(l & (1 << 30))) {      /* F12 = the console's Capture button (once per press) */
        void smo_capture_request(void);
        smo_capture_request();
        return 0;
    }
    if ((m == WM_KEYDOWN || m == WM_SYSKEYDOWN) && !(l & (1 << 30))) {   /* the amiibo menu's key (controllers.ini [hotkeys], F1 by default) */
        int nnpad_hotkey_vk(int which); void amiibo_menu_request(void);
        int vk = nnpad_hotkey_vk(0);
        if (vk && (int)w == vk) { amiibo_menu_request(); return 0; }
    }
    return DefWindowProcA(h, m, w, l);
}

static char g_title[96];

static DWORD WINAPI window_thread(LPVOID arg) {
    (void)arg;
    CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);   /* smo_guide.c: the WebView2 objects live on this thread */
    WNDCLASSA wc;
    memset(&wc, 0, sizeof wc);
    wc.lpfnWndProc = wndproc;
    wc.hInstance = GetModuleHandleA(NULL);
    wc.lpszClassName = "smo_native_window";
    wc.style = CS_OWNDC | CS_DBLCLKS;
    wc.hCursor = LoadCursor(NULL, IDC_ARROW);
    RegisterClassA(&wc);
    /* window mode and size from config\graphics.ini (gfx_options.c). borderless window (the default): frameless,
     * the configured size (at most the primary monitor's work area), centred on it. borderless fullscreen / fullscreen: a
     * frameless window over the primary monitor (fullscreen: also topmost). F11 switches (window_fullscreen). */
    const GfxOptions *go = gfx_options();
    DWORD style = (go->window_mode ? WS_POPUP : WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW) | WS_CLIPCHILDREN;      /* children: the Help page (smo_guide.c) */
    int cw = go->width, ch = go->height, px = CW_USEDEFAULT, py = CW_USEDEFAULT;
    if (go->window_mode) {
        MONITORINFO mi;
        POINT origin = {0, 0};
        memset(&mi, 0, sizeof mi); mi.cbSize = sizeof mi;
        if (GetMonitorInfoA(MonitorFromPoint(origin, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY), &mi)) {
            if (go->window_mode == 3) {
                int ww = mi.rcWork.right - mi.rcWork.left, wh = mi.rcWork.bottom - mi.rcWork.top;
                if (cw > ww) cw = ww;
                if (ch > wh) ch = wh;
                px = mi.rcWork.left + (ww - cw) / 2; py = mi.rcWork.top + (wh - ch) / 2;
            } else { cw = mi.rcMonitor.right - mi.rcMonitor.left; ch = mi.rcMonitor.bottom - mi.rcMonitor.top; px = mi.rcMonitor.left; py = mi.rcMonitor.top; }
        }
    }
    g_win_full = go->window_mode == 1 || go->window_mode == 2;
    g_win_drag = go->window_mode == 3;
    g_win_topmost = go->window_mode == 2;
    RECT r = {0, 0, cw, ch};
    AdjustWindowRect(&r, style, FALSE);
    printf("display: window %s, client %dx%d (graphics.ini; F11 switches between covering the monitor and the window)\n",
           go->window_mode == 2 ? "fullscreen (borderless, topmost)" : go->window_mode == 1 ? "borderless fullscreen" : go->window_mode == 3 ? "borderless window" : "windowed", cw, ch);
    /* Only the copies a person plays (smo_native.exe, smo_user.exe, or SMO_SHOW=1) get a window on screen;
     * test copies started under any other name keep theirs off-screen and out of the taskbar, so automated
     * runs do not cover the desktop. SMO_TITLE names the window. */
    char exe[MAX_PATH] = "";
    GetModuleFileNameA(NULL, exe, sizeof exe);
    const char *base = strrchr(exe, '\\') ? strrchr(exe, '\\') + 1 : exe, *show = getenv("SMO_SHOW");
    int visible = show ? atoi(show) != 0 : (!_stricmp(base, "smo_native.exe") || !_stricmp(base, "smo_user.exe"));
    snprintf(g_title, sizeof g_title, "%s", getenv("SMO_TITLE") ? getenv("SMO_TITLE") : "Super Mario Odyssey (smo-recomp)");
    if (visible)
        g_hwnd = CreateWindowExA(go->window_mode == 2 ? WS_EX_TOPMOST : 0, wc.lpszClassName, g_title, style | WS_VISIBLE, px, py, r.right - r.left,
                                 r.bottom - r.top, NULL, NULL, wc.hInstance, NULL);
    else {
        g_hwnd = CreateWindowExA(WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW | WS_EX_NOACTIVATE, wc.lpszClassName, g_title, style, -32000, -32000,
                                 r.right - r.left, r.bottom - r.top, NULL, NULL, wc.hInstance, NULL);
        ShowWindow(g_hwnd, SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE);
    }
    InterlockedExchange(&g_ready, 1);
    MSG msg;
    while (GetMessageA(&msg, NULL, 0, 0) > 0) { TranslateMessage(&msg); DispatchMessageA(&msg); }
    return 0;
}

/* Signals the guest's vsync event 60 times per second. */
static DWORD WINAPI vsync_thread(LPVOID arg) {
    (void)arg;
    LARGE_INTEGER next;
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&next);
    if (!old_pacing()) {
        LARGE_INTEGER t0 = next, now;
        LONG64 n = 0;
        HANDLE timer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL, 0x00000002 /* CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION */, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
        SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL);
        for (;;) {
            LONGLONG target = t0.QuadPart + (LONGLONG)((double)(n + 1) * (double)g_freq.QuadPart / g_rate);      /* no accumulated rounding */
            QueryPerformanceCounter(&now);
            LONGLONG left = target - now.QuadPart;
            if (left > 0) {
                LARGE_INTEGER due;
                due.QuadPart = -((left - g_freq.QuadPart / 2000) * 10000000 / g_freq.QuadPart);
                if (due.QuadPart < 0) { if (timer && SetWaitableTimer(timer, &due, 0, NULL, NULL, FALSE)) WaitForSingleObject(timer, 100); else Sleep((DWORD)(left * 1000 / g_freq.QuadPart)); }
                for (QueryPerformanceCounter(&now); now.QuadPart < target; QueryPerformanceCounter(&now)) YieldProcessor();
            }
            LONG64 passed = (LONG64)((double)(now.QuadPart - t0.QuadPart) * g_rate / (double)g_freq.QuadPart);   /* >= n + 1; more when this thread was kept off the CPU */
            if (passed < n + 1) passed = n + 1;
            if (passed > n + 1) InterlockedExchangeAdd64(&g_vsync_late, passed - (n + 1));
            n = passed;
            if (g_vsync_event && vsync_signal_ok()) { os_signal_event(g_vsync_event); InterlockedIncrement64(&g_vsync_signals); }
            AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_vsync_lock);
            InterlockedExchange64(&g_vsync_n, n);
            ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_vsync_lock);
            WakeAllConditionVariable(&g_vsync_cv);
            nvn_tl(8 /* TL_VSYNC */, (int)(n & 0xffff));
            vsync_test_key();
        }
    }
    for (;;) {
        next.QuadPart += g_freq.QuadPart / 60;
        LARGE_INTEGER now;
        QueryPerformanceCounter(&now);
        LONGLONG ms = (next.QuadPart - now.QuadPart) * 1000 / g_freq.QuadPart;
        if (ms > 0) Sleep((DWORD)ms); else next = now;
        if (g_vsync_event && vsync_signal_ok()) { os_signal_event(g_vsync_event); InterlockedIncrement64(&g_vsync_signals); }
        vsync_test_key();
    }
}
static void vsync_test_key(void) {
    {
        /* Test aid: SMO_AUTOKEY=<letter>,<first second>,<every n seconds> presses a key now and then, so a run without a person can get
         * past "press any button". Only while this window is the foreground window, so the key never reaches another program. */
        static int key = -1, first, every, tick, down;
        if (key == -1) {
            const char *e = getenv("SMO_AUTOKEY");
            key = 0;
            if (e && e[0]) { key = e[0]; first = 30; every = 5; sscanf(e + 1, ",%d,%d", &first, &every); if (every < 1) every = 1; }
        }
        tick++;
        if (key && down && tick - down >= 8) { keybd_event((BYTE)key, 0, KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, 0); down = 0; }
        else if (key && !down && tick >= first * 60 && (tick - first * 60) % (every * 60) == 0 && ((tick % 600 == 0 ? (void)printf("display: test key wanted, window foreground: %d%c", GetForegroundWindow() == g_hwnd, 10) : (void)0), 1) && (GetForegroundWindow() == g_hwnd || (SetForegroundWindow(g_hwnd), GetForegroundWindow() == g_hwnd))) { keybd_event((BYTE)key, 0, 0, 0); down = tick; printf("display: test key %c pressed at frame tick %d%c", key, tick, 10); }
    }
}

void hitch_init(void); void hitch_pacing(int on);      /* hitch.c: SMO_HITCH */
void display_init(void) {
    QueryPerformanceFrequency(&g_freq);
    /* the console's waits with a time-out (nn::os::TimedWaitEvent, TimedReceiveMessageQueue, timed condition
     * variables: os_threads.c, SleepConditionVariableCS with whole milliseconds) end at the time asked for. At the
     * default Windows timer period they ended at the next 15.6 ms tick, so a thread that polls with a 1 ms time-out ran
     * 64 times per second: the movie player's two feed threads delivered one sample per tick and its pre-roll loop
     * [game 0x71036f27b4, 125 x 10 ms, holding the player's mutex] ran out every time (1.3 s, main thread blocked).
     * SMO_TIMER_PERIOD=<ms> (default 1; 0 = leave the system default). */
    { const char *e = getenv("SMO_TIMER_PERIOD"); int ms = e ? atoi(e) : 1; if (ms > 0) { MMRESULT r = timeBeginPeriod((UINT)ms); printf("display: system timer period %d ms requested (%s)%c", ms, r == TIMERR_NOERROR ? "ok" : "refused", 10); } }
    hitch_init();
    CreateThread(NULL, 0, window_thread, NULL, 0, NULL);
    while (!g_ready) Sleep(1);
    nvn_gl_start(g_hwnd);
    speed_init();
    CreateThread(NULL, 0, vsync_thread, NULL, 0, NULL);
    { void nvn_vk_selftest_hook(void); nvn_vk_selftest_hook(); }      /* nvn_vk.c: SMO_RENDERER=vk SMO_VK_SELFTEST=<frames>, then exit */
}

/* Called after every presented frame (nvn_gl.c has already put it in the window): holds the caller to 60 Hz. */
static volatile LONG g_interval = 1;         /* nvnWindowSetPresentInterval: display refreshes per presented frame (0 = do not wait) */
void display_set_interval(int n) { InterlockedExchange(&g_interval, n < 0 ? 0 : n > 5 ? 5 : n); }
void nvn_pf_pace(LONG64 ticks);            /* nvn_gl.c: timing scopes */
/* SMO_CLOCKSTAT=1: per 600 presented frames, the real time, the vsync signals sent, the refreshes the game counted
 * (its frame counter at 0x710593a440: 600 = one step per presented frame) and the refreshes this thread slept through. */
static LONG64 g_cs_steps, g_cs_hist[4];      /* game steps (1 + refreshes skipped) and the histogram of "refreshes counted since the last present" 0, 1, 2, 3+ */
/* nvn_gl.c, at nvnWindowAcquireTexture: the game's window object is the index pointer - 0x30; + 0x138 = refreshes its
 * VSync Count Thread has counted, + 0x140 = the count at its previous present. Right after this call the game computes
 * steps = max(count - last, 1) (0x710386fc30) and then stores last = count. */
void display_clock_sample(uint64_t index_ptr) {
    if (!g_clockstat || !index_ptr) return;
    uint64_t count = rd64(index_ptr - 0x30 + 0x138), last = rd64(index_ptr - 0x30 + 0x140);
    LONG64 d = (LONG64)(count - last);
    g_cs_steps += d > 1 ? d : 1;
    g_cs_hist[d <= 0 ? 0 : d >= 3 ? 3 : d]++;
}
static void clock_stat(LONG64 n, LARGE_INTEGER now) {
    static LARGE_INTEGER t_last; static LONG64 sig_last, late_last, steps_last, h_last[4];
    if (!g_clockstat || n % 600) return;
    LONG64 sig = g_vsync_signals, late = g_vsync_late;
    if (t_last.QuadPart) printf("clock: frames %lld-%lld real %.3f s, vsync signals %lld (%.2f Hz), game steps %lld = %.2f s of game time, refreshes counted between presents 0:%lld 1:%lld 2:%lld 3+:%lld, slept through by the vsync thread %lld%c", (long long)(n - 600), (long long)n,
        (double)(now.QuadPart - t_last.QuadPart) / (double)g_freq.QuadPart, (long long)(sig - sig_last), (double)(sig - sig_last) * (double)g_freq.QuadPart / (double)(now.QuadPart - t_last.QuadPart), (long long)(g_cs_steps - steps_last), (double)(g_cs_steps - steps_last) / 60.0,
        (long long)(g_cs_hist[0] - h_last[0]), (long long)(g_cs_hist[1] - h_last[1]), (long long)(g_cs_hist[2] - h_last[2]), (long long)(g_cs_hist[3] - h_last[3]), (long long)(late - late_last), 10);
    t_last = now; sig_last = sig; late_last = late; steps_last = g_cs_steps; memcpy(h_last, g_cs_hist, sizeof h_last);
}
/* New pacing, part 1 (nvnQueuePresentTexture, after the frame is in the window): decides the refresh that shows it. */
static void frame_queued(void) {
    static LARGE_INTEGER second_start;
    static LONG64 second_frames;
    LARGE_INTEGER now;
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&now);
    if (!second_start.QuadPart) second_start = now;
    LONG64 n = InterlockedIncrement64(&g_frames);
    second_frames++;
    LONG64 at = g_vsync_n + 1, iv = g_interval;
    if (!iv) at = g_vsync_n;                                       /* interval 0: shown at once, nobody waits */
    else if (at < g_latch + iv) at = g_latch + iv;
    g_latch = at;
    InterlockedExchange(&g_latch_pending, iv != 0);
    clock_stat(n, now);
    {   /* TEST ONLY, SMO_FRAMELOG=<k>: a line "frame-mark: <n>" every k presented frames, to place log events in game frames */
        static int every = -1;
        if (every < 0) { const char *e = getenv("SMO_FRAMELOG"); every = e ? atoi(e) : 0; }
        if (every > 0 && n % every == 0) printf("frame-mark: %lld%c", (long long)n, 10);
    }
    if ((now.QuadPart - second_start.QuadPart) >= g_freq.QuadPart) {
        char title[160];
        if (gfx_options()->overlay && second_frames) {       /* frame_time_overlay = on */
            double ms = (double)(now.QuadPart - second_start.QuadPart) * 1000.0 / (double)g_freq.QuadPart / (double)second_frames;
            printf("frame-time: %.2f ms per frame over the last second (%lld frames)\n", ms, (long long)second_frames);
            snprintf(title, sizeof title, "%s - frame %lld - %lld fps - %.2f ms per frame", g_title, (long long)n, (long long)second_frames, ms);
        } else
        snprintf(title, sizeof title, "%s - frame %lld - %lld fps", g_title, (long long)n, (long long)second_frames);
        SetWindowTextA(g_hwnd, title);
        second_frames = 0;
        second_start = now;
    }
}
/* New pacing, part 2: holds the caller until the refresh that shows the last queued frame. Returns 1 if it waited. */
int display_wait_refresh(void) {
    if (old_pacing() || !InterlockedExchange(&g_latch_pending, 0)) return 0;
    if (g_vsync_n >= g_latch) return 0;
    LARGE_INTEGER a, b;
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&a);
    hitch_pacing(1);
    nvn_tl(6 /* TL_PACE_BEGIN */, (int)(g_latch & 0xffff));
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_vsync_lock);
    while (g_vsync_n < g_latch) SleepConditionVariableSRW(&g_vsync_cv, &g_vsync_lock, 100, 0);
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_vsync_lock);
    nvn_tl(7 /* TL_PACE_END */, (int)(g_vsync_n & 0xffff));
    hitch_pacing(0);
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&b);
    nvn_pf_pace(b.QuadPart - a.QuadPart);
    return 1;
}
/* smo_amiibo.c: the menu's own pace while it holds the game: until the next refresh of the clock (16 ms where there is no
 * refresh clock: SMO_OLD_PACING) */
void display_menu_wait(void) {
    if (old_pacing()) { Sleep(16); return; }
    LONG64 n = g_vsync_n;
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_vsync_lock);
    while (g_vsync_n == n) if (!SleepConditionVariableSRW(&g_vsync_cv, &g_vsync_lock, 100, 0)) break;
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_vsync_lock);
}
/* Before a present: a frame queued earlier that nobody waited for (a caller that does not wait on the window sync). */
void display_before_present(void) {
    static int said;
    if (old_pacing() || !g_latch_pending) return;
    if (!said) { said = 1; printf("display: a present without a wait on the window texture's sync: held at the next present instead%c", 10); }
    display_wait_refresh();
}
void display_pace(void) {
    static LARGE_INTEGER next, second_start;
    static LONG64 second_frames;
    LARGE_INTEGER now;
    if (!old_pacing()) { frame_queued(); return; }
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&now);
    if (!next.QuadPart) { next = now; second_start = now; }
    LONG64 n = InterlockedIncrement64(&g_frames);
    second_frames++;
    clock_stat(n, now);
    next.QuadPart += g_freq.QuadPart * g_interval / 60;
    /* wait until `next` exactly. Sleep(ms) cut the wait to whole milliseconds and, at the default 15.6 ms timer period,
     * could overshoot by a frame; a frame that came late was then followed by frames shown early (up to 100 ms of debt).
     * Now: a high-resolution waitable timer up to 0.5 ms before the deadline, then a spin; a late frame may be made up for
     * by at most one refresh interval, as a display that missed a refresh shows the next frame at the next one. */
    LONGLONG left = next.QuadPart - now.QuadPart, frame_ticks = g_freq.QuadPart * (g_interval ? g_interval : 1) / 60;
    if (!g_interval) next = now;
    else if (left > 0) {
        static HANDLE timer;
        LARGE_INTEGER after, due;
        hitch_pacing(1);
        if (!timer) timer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL, 0x00000002 /* CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION */, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
        due.QuadPart = -((left - g_freq.QuadPart / 2000) * 10000000 / g_freq.QuadPart);          /* relative, 100 ns units */
        if (due.QuadPart < 0) { if (timer && SetWaitableTimer(timer, &due, 0, NULL, NULL, FALSE)) WaitForSingleObject(timer, 100); else Sleep((DWORD)(left * 1000 / g_freq.QuadPart)); }
        for (QueryPerformanceCounter(&after); after.QuadPart < next.QuadPart; QueryPerformanceCounter(&after)) YieldProcessor();
        hitch_pacing(0);
        nvn_pf_pace(after.QuadPart - now.QuadPart);
    } else if (-left > frame_ticks) next.QuadPart = now.QuadPart - frame_ticks;
    if ((now.QuadPart - second_start.QuadPart) >= g_freq.QuadPart) {
        char title[160];
        if (gfx_options()->overlay && second_frames) printf("frame-time: %.2f ms per frame over the last second (%lld frames)\n", (double)(now.QuadPart - second_start.QuadPart) * 1000.0 / (double)g_freq.QuadPart / (double)second_frames, (long long)second_frames);
        if (gfx_options()->overlay && second_frames) snprintf(title, sizeof title, "%s - frame %lld - %lld fps - %.2f ms per frame", g_title, (long long)n, (long long)second_frames, (double)(now.QuadPart - second_start.QuadPart) * 1000.0 / (double)g_freq.QuadPart / (double)second_frames);
        else
        snprintf(title, sizeof title, "%s - frame %lld - %lld fps", g_title, (long long)n, (long long)second_frames);
        SetWindowTextA(g_hwnd, title);
        second_frames = 0;
        second_start = now;
    }
}

long long display_frames(void) { return g_frames; }  /* smo_nerve.c (SMO_STAGE_LIST): frames presented so far */

void display_report(FILE *out) {
    fprintf(out, "\ndisplay: %lld frames presented\n", (long long)g_frames);
    fprintf(out, "display: %s; %lld vsync signals, %lld refreshes slept through by the vsync thread\n", old_pacing() ? "old pacing (SMO_OLD_PACING=1: two clocks)" : "one refresh clock", (long long)g_vsync_signals, (long long)g_vsync_late);
    nvn_gl_report(out);
}

/* ---- nn::vi: one display, one layer; the native window is an opaque token for NVN */
static uint8_t g_display_token[16], g_layer_token[16], g_native_window_token[16];
static void vi_OpenDefaultDisplay(Ctx *c) { wr64(A0, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)g_display_token); RET(0); }
static void vi_CreateLayer(Ctx *c) { wr64(A0, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)g_layer_token); RET(0); }
static void vi_GetNativeWindow(Ctx *c) { wr64(A0, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)g_native_window_token); RET(0); }
static void vi_GetDisplayVsyncEvent(Ctx *c) {         /* (SystemEventType *out, Display *) */
    os_init_event(A0, 1);
    g_vsync_event = A0;
    RET(0);
}

static const ImportDef vi_imports[] = {

```

`runtime/gfx/gfx_options.c`:

```c
/* Graphics options: config\graphics.ini.
 *
 * Path: SMO_GRAPHICS_CONFIG=<file> when set; else graphics.ini beside the file SMO_CONFIG names (SMO_CONFIG is the
 * path of controllers.ini, nnpad_sdl.c); else <exe folder>\..\config\graphics.ini. Written with the defaults and their
 * documentation when it does not exist. Read ONCE at start (the window, the device and the swapchain are made from it).
 * Environment switches of the test scripts (SMO_RENDERER, SMO_VK_DEVICE, SMO_VK_PRESENT) win over the file.
 * The controllers.ini reader of nnpad_sdl.c is built around its device sections and is not reusable here: this file has
 * its own 30-line reader (key = value, ';' or '#' comments, section headers ignored). */
#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "gfx_options.h"

static const char *const k_default_ini =
"; graphics.ini: display and rendering options of the native build (read once at start by gfx_options.c).\r\n"
"; Delete the file to get it written again with these defaults. A line starting with ';' is a comment.\r\n"
"; Every value below is the default; the defaults draw exactly what the game draws on the console.\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; renderer = vulkan | opengl\r\n"
";   vulkan: the default. opengl: the first renderer (NVIDIA only), kept as a fallback.\r\n"
"renderer = vulkan\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; window = borderless_window | borderless_fullscreen | windowed | fullscreen\r\n"
";   borderless_window:     a window without a frame or title bar, the size below, centred on the screen. Drag it\r\n"
";                          anywhere to move it; double-click it for borderless_fullscreen and back.\r\n"
";   borderless_fullscreen: no frame, covers the monitor the window is on (the desktop keeps its resolution).\r\n"
";   windowed:              a normal window with a title bar, the client size below.\r\n"
";   fullscreen:            as borderless_fullscreen, and always on top. (Exclusive fullscreen with a mode change is\r\n"
";                          not implemented.)\r\n"
";   F11 switches between covering the monitor and the window while the game runs.\r\n"
"window = borderless_window\r\n"
"width = 1280\r\n"
"height = 720\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; vsync = clock | on | off | mailbox      (Vulkan)\r\n"
";   clock:   frames are shown at once (mailbox when the GPU offers it, else immediate) and the game is paced by the\r\n"
";            program's own 60 Hz clock. Lowest latency; can tear only when mailbox is missing.\r\n"
";   on:      the display's own vertical sync (FIFO). No tearing; on a display that is not 60 Hz the two clocks drift.\r\n"
";   off:     immediate presentation, tearing allowed. The game still runs at 60 frames per second.\r\n"
";   mailbox: mailbox or nothing (falls back to clock's choice with a message when the GPU does not offer it).\r\n"
"vsync = clock\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; gpu = auto | <number> | <part of the name>      (Vulkan)\r\n"
";   auto: a discrete GPU first, then an integrated one. The log lists the devices with their numbers:\r\n"
";   'nvn_vk: device 0: ...'. Examples: gpu = 1      gpu = Intel      gpu = RTX\r\n"
"gpu = auto\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; console_mode = docked | handheld\r\n"
";   What nn::oe::GetOperationMode answers. Leave it at docked: handheld is not measured on PC.\r\n"
"console_mode = docked\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; resolution_scale = 1.0\r\n"
";   Internal resolution scale, 0.25 to 1.0 (Vulkan only; OpenGL ignores it). 1.0 = the game's 1920x1080. 0.75 = 1440x810,\r\n"
";   0.5 = 960x540: the main switch for a weak GPU. The whole picture is drawn smaller, the 2D interface too (it gets\r\n"
";   softer), and is scaled to the window size.\r\n"
"resolution_scale = 1.0\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; anisotropic_filtering = game | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16      (Vulkan)\r\n"
";   game: each texture sampler keeps the value the game gave it. A number: at least that much on every sampler that\r\n"
";   filters between mip levels (sharper textures at flat angles; changes the picture, costs little on any GPU).\r\n"
"anisotropic_filtering = game\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; shader_wait = hold | skip      (Vulkan)\r\n"
";   What happens when a draw needs a shader or pipeline that is not ready yet (mostly the first time something is shown\r\n"
";   on this PC). hold: the frame waits for it (a late frame, a correct picture). skip: during play the draw is\r\n"
";   left out until it is ready (no late frame; the object or effect is missing for some frames). The log counts both.\r\n"
"shader_wait = hold\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; profile = custom | low\r\n"
";   custom: every key of this file as written. low: the set measured for a weak or integrated GPU (Intel\r\n"
";   integrated: 4.2 ms of GPU time per frame of play instead of 9.0): resolution_scale = 0.5, anisotropic_filtering = game,\r\n"
";   vsync = clock; those three keys of the file are then not used. The log says which profile is active.\r\n"
"profile = custom\r\n"
"\r\n"
"; frame_time_overlay = off | on\r\n"
";   on: the average frame time of the last second in the window title ('.. fps - 16.67 ms per frame') and as a\r\n"
";   'frame-time:' line in the log. (Bars drawn into the picture are not implemented yet.)\r\n"
"frame_time_overlay = off\r\n";

#define GFX_LOW_SCALE 0.5f
#define GFX_LOW_SCALE_TEXT "0.50"
static GfxOptions g_opt;
static INIT_ONCE g_once = INIT_ONCE_STATIC_INIT;

static void trim(char *s) {
    char *e = s + strlen(s);
    while (e > s && (e[-1] == ' ' || e[-1] == '\t' || e[-1] == '\r' || e[-1] == '\n')) *--e = 0;
    char *b = s;
    while (*b == ' ' || *b == '\t') b++;
    if (b != s) memmove(s, b, strlen(b) + 1);
}
static void opt_path(char *out) {
    const char *e = getenv("SMO_GRAPHICS_CONFIG"), *c = getenv("SMO_CONFIG");
    char tmp[MAX_PATH], exe[MAX_PATH];
    if (e && e[0]) { snprintf(out, MAX_PATH, "%s", e); return; }
    if (c && c[0]) {
        snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s", c);
        char *s = strrchr(tmp, '\\'), *s2 = strrchr(tmp, '/');
        if (s2 > s) s = s2;
        if (s) { *s = 0; snprintf(out, MAX_PATH, "%s\\graphics.ini", tmp); } else snprintf(out, MAX_PATH, "graphics.ini");
        return;
    }
    GetModuleFileNameA(NULL, exe, MAX_PATH);
    char *s = strrchr(exe, '\\');
    if (s) *s = 0;
    snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s\\..\\config\\graphics.ini", exe);
    if (!_fullpath(out, tmp, MAX_PATH)) snprintf(out, MAX_PATH, "%s", tmp);
}
static BOOL CALLBACK opt_load(PINIT_ONCE once, PVOID arg, PVOID *ctx) {
    (void)once; (void)arg; (void)ctx;
    GfxOptions *o = &g_opt;
    int written = 0, unknown = 0;
    memset(o, 0, sizeof *o);
    o->width = 1280; o->height = 720; o->scale = 1.0f; o->window_mode = 3;
    opt_path(o->path);
    FILE *f = fopen(o->path, "rb");
    if (!f) {
        char b[MAX_PATH];
        snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%s", o->path);
        for (char *p = b + 3; *p; p++) if (*p == '\\' || *p == '/') { *p = 0; CreateDirectoryA(b, NULL); *p = '\\'; }
        if ((f = fopen(o->path, "wb")) != NULL) { fwrite(k_default_ini, 1, strlen(k_default_ini), f); fclose(f); written = 1; }
        f = fopen(o->path, "rb");
    }
    char line[512];
    while (f && fgets(line, sizeof line, f)) {
        char *eq, *key = line, *val;
        trim(line);
        if (!line[0] || line[0] == ';' || line[0] == '#' || line[0] == '[' || !(eq = strchr(line, '='))) continue;
        *eq = 0; val = eq + 1;
        trim(key); trim(val);
        if (!_stricmp(key, "renderer")) o->renderer = !_stricmp(val, "opengl") || !_stricmp(val, "gl");
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "window")) o->window_mode = !_stricmp(val, "borderless_fullscreen") || !_stricmp(val, "borderless") ? 1 : !_stricmp(val, "fullscreen") ? 2 : !_stricmp(val, "windowed") ? 0 : 3;
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "width")) { int v = atoi(val); if (v >= 320 && v <= 16384) o->width = v; }
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "height")) { int v = atoi(val); if (v >= 180 && v <= 16384) o->height = v; }
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "vsync")) o->present = !_stricmp(val, "on") ? 1 : !_stricmp(val, "off") ? 2 : !_stricmp(val, "mailbox") ? 3 : 0;
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "gpu")) { if (_stricmp(val, "auto")) snprintf(o->gpu, sizeof o->gpu, "%s", val); }
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "console_mode")) o->handheld = !_stricmp(val, "handheld");
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "resolution_scale")) { float v = (float)atof(val); if (v > 0) o->scale = v; }
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "anisotropic_filtering")) { int v = atoi(val); o->aniso = v == 2 || v == 4 || v == 8 || v == 16 ? v : 0; }
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "frame_time_overlay")) o->overlay = !_stricmp(val, "on") || !strcmp(val, "1");
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "profile")) o->profile = !_stricmp(val, "low");
        else if (!_stricmp(key, "shader_wait")) o->shader_skip = !_stricmp(val, "skip");
        else unknown++;
    }
    if (f) fclose(f);
    if (o->profile == 1) {       /* the low-end profile wins over the three keys it sets, wherever they stand in the file */
        o->scale = GFX_LOW_SCALE; o->aniso = 0; o->present = 0;
    }
    printf("graphics profile: %s\n", o->profile == 1 ? "low (weak or integrated GPU): resolution_scale=" GFX_LOW_SCALE_TEXT ", anisotropic_filtering=game, vsync=clock; these three keys of the file are not used"
                                                     : "custom (every key of graphics.ini as written; 'profile = low' is the set for a weak or integrated GPU)");
    static const char *const k_win[4] = {"windowed", "borderless_fullscreen", "fullscreen", "borderless_window"}, *const k_vs[4] = {"clock", "on", "off", "mailbox"};
    printf("graphics options: %s (%s): renderer=%s window=%s %dx%d vsync=%s gpu=%s console_mode=%s resolution_scale=%.2f anisotropic_filtering=%d frame_time_overlay=%s%s\n", o->path,
           written ? "written with the defaults" : f ? "read" : "NOT readable, defaults used", o->renderer ? "opengl" : "vulkan", k_win[o->window_mode], o->width, o->height, k_vs[o->present],
           o->gpu[0] ? o->gpu : "auto", o->handheld ? "handheld" : "docked", o->scale, o->aniso, o->overlay ? "on" : "off", unknown ? " (lines with an unknown key were ignored)" : "");
    if (o->scale != 1.0f && o->renderer) printf("graphics options: resolution_scale=%.2f is ignored by the OpenGL renderer (Vulkan only)\n", o->scale);
    if (o->scale != 1.0f && (o->scale < 0.25f || o->scale > 1.0f)) printf("graphics options: resolution_scale=%.2f is outside 0.25 .. 1.0: the nearest of the two is used\n", o->scale);
    fflush(stdout);
    return TRUE;
}
const GfxOptions *gfx_options(void) {
    InitOnceExecuteOnce(&g_once, opt_load, NULL, NULL);
    return &g_opt;
}

```

`runtime/gfx/gfx_options.h`:

```h
/* Graphics options: config\graphics.ini. See gfx_options.c. */
#ifndef GFX_OPTIONS_H
#define GFX_OPTIONS_H
typedef struct {
    char path[260];
    int renderer;            /* 0 Vulkan (default), 1 OpenGL                               env SMO_RENDERER=vk|gl wins */
    int window_mode;         /* 0 windowed, 1 borderless fullscreen (desktop size), 2 fullscreen (borderless, topmost, covering the
                              * monitor), 3 borderless window (the default: no frame, width x height, centred) */
    int width, height;       /* client size of the windowed modes (windowed, borderless window) */
    int present;             /* 0 clock (mailbox, else immediate, paced by our 60 Hz clock), 1 vsync on (fifo), 2 vsync off (immediate), 3 mailbox;   env SMO_VK_PRESENT wins */
    char gpu[64];            /* "" = discrete first; an index of the printed list, or a part of the device name   env SMO_VK_DEVICE wins */
    float scale;             /* internal resolution scale asked for (Vulkan: nvn_vk_draw.c rs_scale, 0.25 .. 1.0; env SMO_VK_SCALE wins) */
    int handheld;            /* 1: the game is told it runs handheld = it makes its own 1280x720 render targets instead of 1920x1080 */
    int aniso;               /* 0 = the game's own value; 2, 4, 8, 16 = at least that on samplers that filter between mip levels */
    int overlay;             /* 1: frame time in the title bar and a "frame-time:" log line every second */
    int shader_skip;         /* shader_wait: 0 hold (a draw waits for its shader or pipeline: the frame is late), 1 skip (near a scene the draw is left out until they are ready; nvn_vk_pipelines.c skip_on; env SMO_VK_NOHOLD wins) */
    int profile;            /* 0 custom (the keys as written), 1 low: scale, aniso and present are set by the profile (gfx_options.c) */
} GfxOptions;
const GfxOptions *gfx_options(void);      /* any thread; read once (the file is written with defaults when it does not exist) */
#endif

```


`runtime/gfx/mx_translate.c`:

```c
/* Maxwell shader machine code -> GLSL. See mx_translate.h for the conventions shared with nvn_gl.c.
 *
 * How it works
 *   1. Control flow analysis from the entry: every reachable instruction slot is marked; the SSY/PBK/PCNT
 *      token stack is followed statically (as the hardware's per-warp stack, and as suyu's control_flow.cpp),
 *      so SYNC / BRK / CONT become plain jumps to known targets. BRX jump tables are found as suyu does
 *      (LDC from a constant buffer, bounded by SHL + IMNMX) and read from constant buffer 1.
 *   2. Only jump targets start a new "case" of a dispatch switch inside a loop; straight-line code between
 *      them is emitted as ordinary statements (falling through from case to case). A shader without jumps
 *      becomes straight code with no loop at all.
 *   3. Registers are local uints r0..r254 (RZ reads 0u); predicates are bools p0..p6 (PT = true); the
 *      condition code is four global bools (zero, sign, carry, overflow). Float operations bit-cast.
 * Instruction encodings come from suyu's opcode table (mx_ops.h) and the
 * semantics from its translate/impl files. Anything not handled makes the whole shader fail with the instruction's name. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include "mx_translate.h"
#include "mx_ops.h"

#define MXB(x, lo, n) ((unsigned)(((x) >> (lo)) & ((1ull << (n)) - 1)))
#define MAXSTK 16

typedef struct { uint8_t tok[MAXSTK]; uint32_t tgt[MAXSTK]; int n; } Stk;     /* tokens: 1 SSY, 2 PBK, 3 PCNT, 4 PEXIT */
typedef struct {
    const MxIn *in;
    const uint8_t *code;
    unsigned words;
    char *s; size_t len, cap;                 /* body being emitted */
    int fail; char why[200], failop[40];
    uint32_t cbufs, in_attr, out_attr, tex_units, clip_out, ssbos;
    uint8_t regs[256], preds[8], in_comp[32], in_mode[32];
    int uses_gmem, uses_gstore, uses_cc, uses_layer_out, uses_vp_out, uses_psize, uses_lmem, insns, blocks, any_jump, uses_alpha;
    uint8_t *reach, *leader;
    int structured;                           /* jumps emitted as guarded blocks + real loops (plan_structured) instead of the pc switch */
    unsigned *loop_end;                       /* structured: loop_end[T] = last word of the loop whose head is T (0: no loop starts at T) */
    const uint8_t *base;                      /* instruction word 0 (a scheduling word) */
    uint32_t gubos;                           /* compute: uniform buffers reached through global memory */
    unsigned smem_words;
    int uses_smem;
    int uses_fcs, uses_tf, uses_shfl;                    /* MxIn.screen_scale: gl_FragCoord.xy was scaled / a texelFetch was mapped */
    uint32_t images, images_read, images_written;
    uint16_t image_fmt[8]; uint8_t image_type[8];
    uint32_t *jt;                             /* static jump target of SYNC / BRK / CONT */
    Stk *stks; int nstk, capstk;
    uint16_t *stk_of;
    char ring[24][1200]; int ri;
    char exitcode[4096];
    unsigned lmem_words, ssbo_word0;
    struct { uint8_t unit, shadow; uint16_t binding; char type[24]; } smp[64]; int nsmp;      /* target 1: named samplers used (SMP) */
    int dyn_unit_ok;                          /* tex_unit() may return a unit of a handle kept in a uniform buffer (op_tex_b) */
} Mx;

const char *mx_opcode_name(uint64_t insn) {
    for (size_t k = 0; k < sizeof mx_op_table / sizeof mx_op_table[0]; k++)
        if ((insn & mx_op_table[k].mask) == mx_op_table[k].value) return mx_op_name[mx_op_table[k].op];
    return "INVALID";
}
static int decode(uint64_t insn) {
    for (size_t k = 0; k < sizeof mx_op_table / sizeof mx_op_table[0]; k++)
        if ((insn & mx_op_table[k].mask) == mx_op_table[k].value) return mx_op_table[k].op;
    return MXOP_INVALID;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- text */
static void emit(Mx *e, const char *fmt, ...) {
    va_list ap;
    if (e->len + 4096 > e->cap) { e->cap = e->cap * 2 + 65536; e->s = realloc(e->s, e->cap); }
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    e->len += (size_t)vsnprintf(e->s + e->len, e->cap - e->len, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
}
static const char *S(Mx *e, const char *fmt, ...) {      /* formatted temporary (ring of buffers) */
    char *b = e->ring[e->ri++ % 24];
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    vsnprintf(b, sizeof e->ring[0], fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    return b;
}
static void fail(Mx *e, const char *op, const char *fmt, ...) {
    va_list ap;
    if (e->fail) return;
    e->fail = 1;
    snprintf(e->failop, sizeof e->failop, "%s", op);
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    vsnprintf(e->why, sizeof e->why, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- operands */
static const char *X(Mx *e, unsigned r) { if (r == 255) return "0u"; e->regs[r] = 1; return S(e, "r%u", r); }
static const char *D(Mx *e, unsigned r) { if (r == 255) return "rz"; e->regs[r] = 1; return S(e, "r%u", r); }
static const char *CB(Mx *e, uint64_t i) {                /* c[bits 34..38][bits 20..33 words] */
    unsigned b = MXB(i, 34, 5), w = MXB(i, 20, 14);
    if (b == 0 && w >= e->ssbo_word0 && w < e->ssbo_word0 + 64) {     /* NVN storage buffer descriptor {address, size}: a tagged fake address */
        unsigned k = (w - e->ssbo_word0) / 4, f = (w - e->ssbo_word0) & 3;
        if (f == 0) { e->ssbos |= 1u << k; return S(e, "0x%08xu", (k + 1) << 27); }
        return f == 2 ? "0x07fffffcu" : "0u";
    }
    if (b == 0 && e->in->stage == MX_COMPUTE && w >= 0x210 / 4 && w < 0x210 / 4 + 60) {
        /* compute: the descriptor {address, size} of uniform buffer n, at c0 byte 0x210 + 16n. The compute engine has 8 constant
         * buffer slots only, so the game's compiler reaches the uniform buffers that do not fit (seen: 6, 7, 8) through global
         * memory (LDG). Tag 17 + n; mx_ldg reads the same block the constant buffer path uses (c3 + n). */
```
